statement.subject: commit:edaf91650884d8b2710a48fedfe61237610a8023
statement.object: restore VQL sidecar reading broken by module __getattr__
statement.text: fix(vdisplay-client): restore VQL sidecar reading broken by module __getattr__

source.rawExcerpt:
fix(vdisplay-client): restore VQL sidecar reading broken by module __getattr__
Commit e4632c27 swept up an intermediate state of the vdisplay.vql extraction
in which the moved readers were re-exported through a module-level PEP 562
__getattr__. That only fires for module.attr access, never for LOAD_GLOBAL
inside the module itself, so every internal caller raised NameError. The broad
except Exception in load_vql_metadata swallowed it and returned zero
ui_elements: imports green, data silently wrong.

Replace the __getattr__ with explicit wrapper functions that import
vdisplay.vql on call. This keeps three properties at once: import koru works
where vdisplay is absent (it is an optional extra), internal global lookups
resolve, and monkeypatch.setattr on this module still works for the tests.

Also record in the boundary proposal that its ~60-70% shrink estimate for
vdisplay_client.py does not survive measurement (~1100 of 6635 lines are
vdisplay-bound), plus the two implementation traps hit here.

Verified: koru 3525 passed / 0 failed; vdisplay 813 passed / 0 failed.

Co-authored-by: Koru Agent <agent@coru.dev>

source.rawExcerpt:
refactor(queue): split parse_lifecycle_request god-function (CC 38 -> 12)
parse_lifecycle_request was one 90-line if/elif chain, one branch per lifecycle
command, each with its own option validation — CC 38, the worst in koru and a
regix hard-gate violation.

Split into a flat dispatcher plus per-command validators: _parse_claim,
_parse_fail, _parse_ready, and a data table _MAPPED_LIFECYCLE_COMMANDS for the
three commands (start, done/complete, block) whose kwargs are a plain
flag->snake_case map, factored through _snake_kwargs/_mapped_request. The
dispatcher is now CC 12, every helper <= 8; regix hard CC violations 8 -> 7,
planfile_sdk no longer listed.

Behaviour-preserving: added characterisation tests first for the branches the
suite never covered (block, the complete alias, short/long flag collisions,
lease-seconds parse failure, empty ticket id), confirmed green on the old code,
then refactored. 399 planfile/lifecycle/queue tests pass.

Co-authored-by: Koru Agent <agent@coru.dev>

statement.subject: commit:7b9021de42ae59f06a404c784978418798f32947
statement.object: name the waiting_input skip instead of reporting unknown
statement.text: fix(autonomy): name the waiting_input skip instead of reporting unknown

source.rawExcerpt:
fix(autonomy): name the waiting_input skip instead of reporting unknown
The autonomous loop parked on a human/operator ticket (STARTER-012,
queue=waiting_input) reported decided=skip:unknown / because[unknown] 'No
structured reason recorded' every cycle — for a state it fully understands.

Root cause: stuck_waiting_input is defined in SKIP_CODE_DESCRIPTIONS and
consumed by operator_loop_quick_actions, but classify_skip_code only emits it
from the autopilot skip path (via the autopilot_skipped_stuck_status flag).
With --no-autopilot, or a human ticket the loop can never drive, that flag is
never set, so the code fell through to 'unknown' — a defined, consumed, but
never-produced reason code.

build_decision_record already has this exact fallback for the idle mirror case
(unknown + idle + no ticket -> idle_no_ticket); this adds the waiting_input
mirror (unknown + waiting_input + real ticket -> stuck_waiting_input).
_skip_because already handles the stuck_ prefix, so the operator now gets
'queue stuck on waiting_input ticket=STARTER-012; waiting ticket is not
llm-ready' instead of 'unknown', and the stuck_waiting_input quick-actions
finally fire.

Verified end-to-end against the live loop; 64 decision/cycle tests pass.

Co-authored-by: Koru Agent <agent@coru.dev>

statement.subject: commit:755395acff377aaafe99436162b3730749f93bf6
statement.object: move IDE chat-target scoring out of koru
statement.text: refactor(koruide): move IDE chat-target scoring out of koru

source.rawExcerpt:
refactor(koruide): move IDE chat-target scoring out of koru
photo_vql_target.py was filed in the boundary proposal under 'vdisplay owns
screen truth'. Measuring it says otherwise: 31 of its 34 functions (383 lines)
encode where JetBrains puts its composer, how a VS Code-family top chat differs
from a status bar, and what a plausible input box looks like. None of that is a
fact about a screen; all of it is a fact about an IDE, which is koruide's
domain. The file reads VQL layers, which is why it looked like vdisplay's — the
proposal assigned it by what it talks to instead of what it knows.

Scoring now lives in koruide/chat_target.py; koru's file drops 525 -> 79 lines
and becomes a binding layer.

Three functions stayed in koru because they describe koru, not any IDE: the
vocabularies that recognise koru's own terminal output inside a capture
(KORU_, DRY_RUN, Polish operator prompts) and vql_candidates_polluted. koru
registers them via set_label_noise_tokens() rather than letting koruide import
them - the same injection idiom koruide.__init__ already uses for its activity
sink. With nothing registered the penalties are zero, so koruide stays usable
standalone: verified in a clean venv with koru absent, where a noisy label
scored -730 before registration and -6730 after.

Tests: 94 passed (chat-target, photo-VQL drive, koruide-standalone, IDE-map).
The 9-11 failures in test_autopilot_daemon.py are pre-existing flakiness -
confirmed by running that file on HEAD without this change (9 failures) and by
its zero references to chat_target or photo_vql.

Co-authored-by: Koru Agent <agent@coru.dev>

statement.subject: commit:ff2816a3f5368e231d156855d772a86348b21910
statement.text: refactor(monitors): move display topology to vdisplay.monitors

source.rawExcerpt:
refactor(monitors): move display topology to vdisplay.monitors
photo_vql_monitor.py was monitor topology — which physical screen an IDE
surface lives on, DP-* ranking, geometry-equal output matching. That is a fact
about displays, so it moved to vdisplay.monitors. koru's file drops 376 -> 95
lines and becomes a binding layer.

Unlike photo_vql_target (which the proposal mis-filed as vdisplay's but
measured as IDE knowledge for koruide), this file really was vdisplay's — the
proposal got this one right.

koru keeps two things that are its own contract, not a display fact:
- KORU_VDISPLAY_SOURCE: koru reads its own variable and forwards the value as
  vdisplay's explicit_source parameter; the resolver no longer touches the
  environment itself.
- format_wayland_vdisplay_operator_hint: a koru-CLI hint (koru autopilot
  vdisplay-up, the koru dashboard on :8765, KORU_ALLOW_BLIND_KEYBOARD_FALLBACK)
  that describes koru, kept in full.

The six surface-preference tests moved to vdisplay with the topology; koru
keeps four tests for its binding (env override read + forwarded, fail-closed
for a disconnected monitor, re-exports resolve).

Depends on vdisplay c00a7a24. Full koru suite: 3512 passed; the 11 failures are
test_autopilot_daemon.py flakiness (0-11 across this session, zero references
to monitors or photo_vql), not this change.

Co-authored-by: Koru Agent <agent@coru.dev>

statement.text: docs(boundary): withdraw the gillm input-chain move as specified

source.rawExcerpt:
docs(boundary): withdraw the gillm input-chain move as specified
Section 2 promised moving the _type_text_at_vql_coords chain into
gillm.injection.strategies as 'generic input actuation'. Measured on the
current tree it is 703 lines across 17 functions that orchestrate three
providers — vdisplay.input.linux_ydotool for clicks, vdisplay.control (or the
agent RPC fallback) for AT-SPI, gillm's Injector for paste/type — plus koru's
own IDE-map targeting and telemetry, and it calls 15 sibling functions in
vdisplay_client.py.

Moving it into gillm would make gillm depend on vdisplay, inverting the very
layering this document exists to fix. gillm already owns the generic half
(Injector.type_text, select_backend, window guard); what is left in koru is
the cross-provider orchestration, which is koru's job.

Re-specified the remaining question instead: whether gillm's Injector should
grow a coordinate-targeted entry point. That is an interface change in gillm,
not a code move out of koru. STARTER-561 updated with the same finding.

Co-authored-by: Koru Agent <agent@coru.dev>

statement.subject: commit:b949abfb98e9713760623e034a7d19fe062c99d0
statement.text: refactor(queue): split CapabilityContract.evaluate into refusal predicates (CC 21 -> 3)

source.rawExcerpt:
refactor(queue): split CapabilityContract.evaluate into refusal predicates (CC 21 -> 3)
evaluate was a linear chain of eight independent guard clauses — actor,
capability, risk, workspace root, denied paths, allow-path escape, file count,
patch size — CC 21, a regix hard-gate violation and the second-worst function
in koru.

Each guard became a side-effect-free _refuse_* method returning a refusing
ContractDecision or None; evaluate is now a flat first-non-None loop over the
eight, CC 3. Behaviour is identical (any single violation still refuses the
whole, first violation wins); the guards are pure so evaluating them eagerly
changes nothing observable. regix hard CC violations 8 -> 5 across the session;
contracts.py is now clean.

384 contract/queue tests pass.

Co-authored-by: Koru Agent <agent@coru.dev>
